title: Willow vs Dragon: Best Dictation October 2026
summary: Willow Voice vs Dragon Professional: compare accuracy, Mac support, and team pricing in October 2026 to choose the right dictation app.
body_markdown:
[Dragon dictation software](https://willowvoice.com/) has been the default answer to voice dictation for decades, so lawyers, physicians, and executives still reach for it first. But a developer splitting the week between a Windows workstation and a MacBook, a clinician dictating notes on an iPhone between patients, and an IT lead rolling dictation out to a team of forty all hit the same wall: a tool built around one user on one machine does not match how work moves today. This comparison covers where Dragon Professional still holds up and where its architecture creates friction, plus differences in speed, setup, pricing, and compliance worth checking before you buy.


**Willow Voice is the better pick over Dragon Professional for most professionals and teams in 2026: it runs natively on Mac, Windows, and iOS at ~200ms latency with 98%+ accuracy, while Dragon runs on Windows only.** Dragon Professional remains a strong choice for one Windows user with a well-trained voice profile on a single machine, but Dragon Professional has no Mac or iOS app and no shared team vocabulary. Teams on mixed hardware get shared custom dictionaries, admin controls, and SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance from Willow Voice.

## What Is Dragon Professional?


Dragon Professional,[made by Nuance (now part of Microsoft)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon_NaturallySpeaking) , runs on Windows only and is built around a locally installed speech recognition engine that trains to your voice over time. Lawyers and executives who record briefs and reports by voice have relied on Dragon, and clinicians often use the separate Dragon Medical product for clinical notes, because its voice profiles improve with use, and that local processing model means audio never leaves the machine, which appeals to users who want data kept off the cloud entirely, a concern covered in depth in our[voice dictation privacy and data security guide](https://willowvoice.com/blog/voice-dictation-security-privacy-guide) .


The trade-offs are real, though. Dragon requires a one-time purchase of about $699 for Dragon Professional v16, a local installation, and an initial voice training period before accuracy stabilizes, with no Mac support, no iOS app for Dragon Professional (Dragon Anywhere is a separate mobile subscription), and no team-wide vocabulary sharing or admin controls. It is a single-user desktop tool built around local processing on one Windows machine, and that architecture shapes both its strengths and its limits.


## What Is Willow Voice?


Willow Voice is built for professionals who need fast, accurate voice input across every app they use, from voice prompting Cursor, Claude, and Gemini to high-volume email, clinical notes, and legal drafts, and it ranks among the best[AI dictation tools](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-ai-powered-dictation-tools) for that range of work. It runs natively on Mac, Windows, and iOS at ~200ms latency, and Auto-Dictionary learns your names, terminology, and corrections over time, so accuracy improves without manual setup. The result is 98%+ accuracy, with 3x fewer errors than built-in tools.


### Built for Teams, Beyond Individual Users


Willow stands apart from most dictation software at the organizational level, which matters when choosing the right[voice dictation for enterprise teams](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-voice-dictation-for-enterprise-teams) . Shared custom dictionaries let teams standardize terminology across every member's device without per-user setup, a capability that sets leading[dictation software tools](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-dictation-software-tools) apart from legacy options. Admin controls push vocabulary changes org-wide without touching individual installs, and team leaderboards surface usage and time-saved data so leads can see where voice adoption is taking hold. SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance mean org-wide rollout fits within existing enterprise security requirements, and a signed BAA is part of the Enterprise tier.


For mixed-device teams running across Windows, Mac, and iOS, vocabulary and settings carry over without per-device setup. A clinician moving between a Windows desktop and an iPhone on rounds, or a developer switching between a Windows workstation and a MacBook at home, works from the same configuration.


## Speed and Latency


A[Stanford study of speech versus typing](https://news.stanford.edu/stories/2016/08/stanford-study-speech-recognition-faster-texting) found speech input about three times faster than typing on a phone, so at 150 WPM speaking versus 40 WPM typing, even a few hundred milliseconds of delay per sentence compounds across a day of emails and documents.


In our own latency benchmark of consumer dictation tools, Willow Voice returned text fastest across short, average, and long dictations. Dragon publishes no latency figure and was not part of this test.


### The Impact on Mixed-Hardware Teams


-


Dragon's local processing ties speed to the machine it runs on, so results are uneven across a team by default, a limitation compared to the best[dictation software for Windows](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-dictation-software-windows) available today.


-


Willow's cloud-based processing gives every user a response typically about 200ms on a stable connection, old laptop or new workstation alike.


-


Dragon's speed depends on each machine running it, while Willow's cloud processing is far less dependent on local hardware to deliver consistent speed at scale.


## Setup, Personalization, and Cross-Platform Support


Getting Dragon Professional to accurate output takes real upfront work: initial voice training, manual profile creation, application-specific vocabulary setup, and ongoing correction sessions to maintain gains. Profiles move between machines only through manual export and import, so a new Windows workstation usually means redoing some of that calibration.[Dragon's Mac version was discontinued in 2018](https://www.speakmac.app/blog/dragon-dictation-alternative-for-mac) and never replaced, and Dragon Professional has no iOS app, which makes[dictation software for Mac](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-voice-dictation-software-mac) a separate consideration entirely.


Willow's learning model runs in the background. Auto-Dictionary picks up names, technical terms, company jargon, and email contacts through normal use, with no training sessions or manual profile setup required. Accuracy improves from the first session and gets sharper over time.


### How This Scales to Teams


Shared custom dictionaries mean vocabulary built by one admin applies to every member from day one, across every supported device. One rollout covers Windows workstations, Mac laptops, and iPhones, all running from the same admin configuration, while Dragon relies on manual profile export and import per user.


## Team Features, Pricing, and Total Cost of Ownership


Dragon Professional v16 starts at approximately $699 for a one-time Windows license, plus[upgrade fees](https://www.getvoibe.com/resources/dragon-pricing/) for major versions, unlike modern[professional voice dictation software](https://willowvoice.com/blog/best-voice-dictation-software-mac-windows) priced on flexible monthly plans. There is no free tier, no shared vocabulary layer, and no admin dashboard. Sharing terminology across a team means manually exporting a voice profile from one machine and importing it on another, person by person, so each setup stays siloed with no org-level adoption visibility.


Willow Voice's Team plan runs $10 per user per month billed annually ($12 billed monthly) and includes shared custom dictionaries, shared shortcuts, admin controls, and team leaderboards that surface words spoken and time saved across the group.[SOC 2 Type II](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/landing/system-and-organization-controls-soc-suite-of-services) compliance and zero data retention apply across all plan tiers, Willow Voice is HIPAA compliant, and a signed business associate agreement (BAA) is available on the Enterprise tier. A genuinely unlimited free plan with no word cap and no credit card required lets any team try the full experience first.


The gap compounds at scale. A 10-person team on Dragon pays roughly $6,990 upfront, plus upgrade fees, with no shared infrastructure. The same team on Willow's annual Team plan runs $1,200 in year one, with shared dictionaries and admin controls included, and stays at that rate without upgrade cycles. By year three, Dragon's total is higher and the team still has no centralized vocabulary layer or admin visibility.


## Why Willow Voice Is the Better Choice


Dragon Professional earns its reputation among a narrow buyer profile: a Windows-only individual with years invested in a trained voice profile and no need to share vocabulary, manage a team, or work across devices. For that person, the local processing model still delivers. Outside that profile, the structural gaps start to matter.


### Where Dragon's Architecture Creates Friction


These constraints come from how Dragon was built:


-


No single rollout across Mac, Windows, and iOS; the architecture is Windows-primary by design.


-


No built-in shared vocabulary; each voice profile stays individual, so team terminology needs manual coordination.


-


Local processing keeps audio on the machine, a real strength for data residency, though IT should confirm current SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA documentation with Nuance.


-


Latency depends on the machine, so speed varies across a team of mixed-age hardware.


Willow Voice covers those gaps: it runs on Mac, Windows, and iOS at ~200ms latency, with shared custom dictionaries, admin controls, and team leaderboards on the Team plan at $10 per user per month, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance from the first session, and 98%+ accuracy with no training required. If your workflow is Windows-only and deeply individual, Dragon may still fit, but for most professionals and teams in 2026, Willow Voice matches how work actually happens. ## FAQs


### Who should choose Willow Voice over Dragon Professional in 2026?


Willow Voice fits professionals on Mac, Windows, and iOS, teams that need shared vocabulary and admin controls, and anyone who wants accurate dictation without voice training. Dragon Professional suits a Windows-only individual with a trained voice profile and no need to share terminology.


### What is the core difference between how Willow Voice and Dragon Professional handle accuracy over time?


Dragon builds accuracy through voice training and manual calibration, and those gains move between machines only through manual profile export and import. Willow's Auto-Dictionary learns your names, technical terms, and corrections through normal use, and that vocabulary carries across Mac, Windows, and iOS without per-device setup.


### Can Dragon Professional support a mixed-device team running Windows, Mac, and iOS?


No. Dragon Professional has no Mac or iOS app, so anyone not on Windows is left out. Willow Voice runs natively on all three platforms, with shared custom dictionaries and admin controls that push vocabulary changes org-wide from a single configuration.


### How does Willow Voice's pricing compare to Dragon Professional's total cost of ownership for a team?


Dragon Professional costs about $699 per Windows license, adds upgrade fees for major versions, and offers no team infrastructure. Willow's Team plan runs $10 per user per month billed annually and includes shared dictionaries, admin controls, team leaderboards, and SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA compliance with zero data retention.


### Is Willow Voice's latency advantage meaningful in practice, or only in benchmarks?


Dragon publishes no latency figure and was not part of our benchmark, but the architecture still matters. Willow's cloud processing targets about 200ms on a normal connection, while Dragon's local processing ties speed to each machine's hardware, so speed can vary across a team.


## Final Thoughts on Dragon Dictation Software vs. Modern Alternatives


[Dragon dictation software](https://willowvoice.com/) holds up for a Windows-only individual with a deeply trained profile. The moment a team spans Mac and Windows, needs shared terminology, or runs on mixed hardware, those structural gaps, no shared vocabulary and speed tied to each machine, show up fast.
